reviews.review:
Updated Review for November 2021
So I've given the game another chance, picked it up on a sale recently nearly 1 year after i bought it originally.
I can say that it has come very far from its release. Most of my concerns i wrote have been fixed.
Gone is the weird blur that made you feel uncomfortable, finally can you enjoy the decent looking graphics and environments.
Explosions especially are looking great.
Hit feedback has also gotten much better and they implemented gore which is a must have if you kill zombies and bug mutants.
Sprinting and movement is much faster, and your stamina bar is much higher. So you can finally now evade and run to your objectives in time.
Also your health feels better, you arent so easily one shotet , but i still dont like the fact that most enemies can hit you proned or stun lock you. (especially zombies do that even the basic ones) This fact makes close combat or melee attacks(warrior class is mostly affected) very annoying, i feel that dogs and later other enemies that can knock you down is enough, and normal enemies should need to hit you 3+ times to prone you.
I've completed all missions that are available so far Solo, so the game is not a coop must.
Also the enemy count has gotten up, which feels much better and the combat more intense, if you play on hard it cranks up enemy count to 11. But the enemy spawning behind you at cleared areas feels terrible, it makes tactical retreats often impossible. You run away from a horde and just back to another horde that just spawned behind you, i think this spawning system should be reworked and cleared areas should stay empty for at least 3-5 minutes.
You still need to run to the helicopter in every mission, but the timer high enough and you can run fast and for a long time, so its fine i guess. I dont really like the helicopter extraction i wish i would just end the mission after finishing the last objective, but i would recommend putting in a helicopter call button to every mission, some of them have it, but most dont. Then you can choose if you still wanna explore or finish the mission, and arent forced to run to the extraction.
Loot is interesting if not a bit basic, most weapon enhancements are vertical progression where you get for example better and better magazines that increase some base stats, just with higher numbers. But what i like is the Chip system, which you can get by completing the new mech missions, you can wear 6 chips on every weapon and the grant you interesting buffs. Those 2 systems are fine to upgrade your weapon but i hope they get more elaborate and we get much more Chips to wear. Things like ammo types, switchable fire rate, upgradeable and different sidearms or even a secondary main weapon would be perfect.
The loot boxes that can drop rare items is also a good addition, now we need also pylons that give you temporary buffs.
Every class has its own skill tree and active and passives skills. I think most are fun and interesting and serve a good role if you play as a team. I just hope we can exchange actives and passives later, get more choices, and maybe a bigger skill tree.
Walking animation really needs and overhaul, when you are in the base in 3rd person its very obvious how bad it is, the upper and lower body arent in sync and very stiff.
In the base we can see cybernetics and big guns like the flamethrower and minigun, i hope we can choose them in a loadout. Maybe for a new class. And cybernetics to upgrade our classes even further.
The new Mech system/missions are interesting, the mech gameplay feels good and is fun to play with, but the mission is very boring, it much rather would play in open maps and do objectives with them. It also needs higher hit points, and it should become customizable.
The weapons we got are fine and the upgrade to them feel somewhat meaningful, now we just need more of them. There are just too few choices in each category, and i think there should be even more, maybe special weapons like energy, plasma, explosives ect. its a zombie/bug alien mutant game, so the devs could go wild.

Overall i would say the game is finally worth playing now, it has a good amount of content and is a neat twin stick/ lite Arpg shooter, that can be played solo or coop.
There are so many good concepts in the game, now it just needs more content of what it already got. More weapons, more gadgets more skills, more customization. 
And i hope we get an endless grinding system like greater rifts from diablo later on.
The game had an really bad launch but now i would say its in a promising state and has gotten a lot of patches/content and wasnt abandoned like many other EA titles.

My old review:

an interesting idea and a good foundation,
BUT
it feels so barren and very un polished, i know its an Early Access. But my eyes literally hurt now because the image is so blurry even on the highest settings that i cant continue to play.
Stamina bar for sprinting should be much higher and sprinting should actually be sprinting not jogging, especially because at the end of every mission they want you to run to a helicopter in a time limit, sorry but that design and repetition is retarded.
The animations of your abilities look very bland and boring and clunky. The ammo count for shotguns is too low. 
Its a twin stick/Arpg shooter where you kill zombies and bugs, but no gore or blood? it feels so bad, as if my abilities and guns have no impact.
The Players health should be much higher and there should be much more enemies, the first missions feel so lifeless and boring, and while you pick up mission objectives, enemies just spawn 5 meters from you and interrupt you nonestop, such a weird design, at least make them come from afar and in waves or something.
Put crates with loot drops and enemies/harder enemies with loot drops , its one of the most important ways to keep me playing hundreds if not thousands of hours in such a game. Dont only make everything blueprint based and make materials  drop from enemies and loot boxes.
I feel very reminded of Helldivers, so if i want to scratch that itch its a much better solution, but i really hope ZCrew can make their own type of game, i think it should be much more solo oriented , BECAUSE listen indie developers, you gonna kill your first game if you make it mainly online coop oriented, even big studios often struggle with a playerbase, so stop focus on multiplayer, your game will fail because no playerbase-> unplayable, make the game  easy soloable and coop optional, otherwise you gonna have a very bad time.
I would recommend make the gameplay much more loot oriented and soloable thats enough to establish a solid dedicated playerbase who loves to grind away, and then implement more content and polish, maybe an more elaborate skill tree for each class so they can play solo if they choose so.

ZCREW（Z字特遣队）
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~

Zcrew is a fun top-down, action-adventure shooter. Zcrew’s story revolves around a post-apocalyptic world full of chaos and mysteries. 

With constant content updates and bug fixes, Zcrew is shaping into a fun top-down CO-OP. 

Plot: At the time of writing this review, Zcrew’s plot is still in a disarray. But one thing is very clear, the planet Earth has suffered a major apocalyptic event.

A great loss of life has occurred, strange creatures, mutated animals and zombie’s now inherit most of the Earth.

It is now up to a select group of elites to reclaim planet Earth back, with any means necessary.  

Gameplay: Zcrew’s is bringing in a traditional top-down shooter configuration but with a few gameplay twists. 

Using WASD for basic movement and E for interaction. So far the game seemed pretty normal but far from it.

As I progressed and leveled up my character class, I started to unlock character-specific abilities and attributes, which they are calling talents. 

Each character comes with different abilities of four in a set. Each ability is locked behind a level. After unlocking there was no need to go back and unlock them, they just started working. 

Throughout my play throw I mostly used the Assault class, it seems like apart from the different abilities there is no other difference between the classes as of yet. And there are no character states involved yet. Which is fine by me one less thing to worry about. 

There are currently four classes in-game, which are Assault, Warrior, Supply, Medic. 

As you select a mission, you will be thrown right into combat with a specific mission and a set of objectives. The missions and all the objectives were linear. Do an objective and move on to the next. I wished there were some dynamic elements thrown into the missions like something went wrong and now the game is pushing me into a corner to figure out what to do next. 

Combat: The combat system of Zcrew is mostly similar to another top-down zombie shooter other than its unique world design and character abilities. 

The combat seemed straight forward at first with its left click to fire, right to melee, and 1-3 to change weapons. 

But where things get interesting is when you start to unlock your abilities and attributes. For example, I mostly played with the assault class, which comes with four abilities, which are – 

1.	Flash: Short distance teleportation 
2.	Lighting ball: Which has a wrong description in-game and is a plasma ball attack. 
3.	Mines: Which throws a set of land mines in a general direction.  
4.	Combat Drone: Spawns a combat drone that will tag along which you and fight. 

Like this, there are three more classes in-game and all are unlocked from the beginning. And each comes with their own unique abilities. 

For the most part, combat seemed straight enough with quite a few unique enemies’ types to deal with from Zombies to mutated spiders. Each type attacks at a predictable style which makes them easy to deal with at the beginning but as their numbers increase it gets very hard very quickly. 

Can be dealt with a decent throw of a Grande, plasma ball, or mines but weirdly enough the mines de-spawned after I looked away. 

Weapon: There are quite a few different weapons in-game that you can use. But most of them felt unbalanced or poorly planned. 

Most guns in-game seemed to be worse than the default one in a way or another. 

Most games provide you with only upgrades as you unlock more weapons or are allowed to craft new ones. But Zcrew went on a different path and is giving the players a chance of downgrading!!!!!

Guns mostly played out and sounded okay but the reload speeds were bad even with the talent selection of faster reload. 

Zcrew is also providing weapons attachments; every weapon except the sidearm gets attachments. Each attachment gives the weapon a state boost of a limited percentage. 

UI: In-game UI is just horrible and overly complicated. The in-game UI is divided into 5 terminals.

For example, you cannot equip your crafted weapons from the crafting terminal nor from the personal inventory terminal. 

You will have to do that from the character terminal!!! 

Another, you cannot dismantle a weapon from your crafting terminal and you have to do it from your personal inventory terminal!!!!

Well, it improved over the course of updates, previously you had to select missions from the mission terminal and then go to a different area to start the mission. It's an improvement, more is required. 

World design: I must say the game nails the post-apocalyptic theme with its empty and desolate environment. I got actually upset looking at the world is such a manner. 

The creators did a good job at map designed but the colors and the foliage looked bad and needs a good retouching. 

Sound effects and music: Decent music selection fits the game nicely. Decent sound effects but needs more work to be put into. 

Weapon sounds effects needs a retouch as well. 

Considering all aspects of the game, I very much enjoyed it, even with all the issues involved. Happy to see that the game is getting constant updates and fixes. 

Positives: 

+ Decent top-down gameplay 
+ Theme appropriate world design 
+ Four character classes with a unique set of abilities
+ Decent crafting system 
+ Well designed good amount of enemy types 
+ Co-op up to four players 

Negatives: 

- Unplanned UI design 
- Sound effects needs some work 
- Color correction is needed 
- Minor bugs and issues 
- Linear missions and objectives 

Embark on a mission with Earth's elites and reclaim the land that was once inhabited by humanity. Zcrew is shaping into a fun top-down co-op shooter, but needs a lot of work to be put into.
6/10

I will start by saying, I never play top down or twin stick shooters, I have never been a console fan.

Now with that said, this game was a very pleasant surprise, Zcrew runs very nice for me on a RX 5500 XT, very smooth game play.  I don't know where people are talking about optimization problems.

Bugs:  The game came out on Dec 17th, not even a month old, Only bug I have encountered is some times when returning to the lobby the game locks but not the whole PC but still requires hard reboot to get out of it. ( hopefully gets fixed soon )

There are 2 classes to start and 2 to unlock later, all classes are unique and feel different.
During missions you collect money, crafting resources and blueprints, these are for crafting new and better weapons / attachments. 
I really like the amount of upgrades for the characters and their weapons, hope this keeps expanding but plenty is there for a early access game not even month old.

I don't ever really write reviews but I thought it was needed for this game, its a very fun co op game and it offers plenty of challenge for 2 people.

I been having blast but don't buy a twin stick shooter and expect 1000 hours of gameplay before your bored and leave bad review, that just makes u the fool.

the game is good except that you cant turn off the ridiculous end of mission timer considering at the end of every mission your swarmed and are only given 30 secs to get to da chopper needs to have the option of either extending or removing that bs timer then it would be worth recommending until then its just annoying rather then enjoyable

Great game that is still getting it's finishing touches, look past the small issues with the settings and I think you will enjoy the gameplay if you like shooters with some perks. I had fun playing by myself and will for sure have even more fun playing with my friends in the future! It's a great style for a game to be played at a birds eye view and be a shooter. Reminds me of old flash games with alot better quality.
You have a stamina bar for sprinting

The game is super fun in co-op!

It does have alot of bugs here and there at it's current state, and it's also a bit confusing in the beginning to learn the menus and everything at the central hub.

But the game looks great and is fun to play, especially in co-op. I hope it will get alot more polished, get more content and more customization with new outfits and skins. Also hope it gets more players to randomly play with because biggest issue for me right now is to find people to play with.

I had a ton of fun so far so i will recommend it, if you can co-op play with random people online or with friends.
